records.name: Arnolds
records.facts_used: Arnolds: The name belongs to the Arnolds/Arnold family. Its Germanic elements are arn, eagle, and walt, power, associated with ruling. These old components explain the compound’s linguistic history rather than predicting a bearer’s character. The Latvian Language Agency gives the exact rendering Arnold → Arnolds, citing page 59 of a 1960 manual. This dated record illustrates transmission between languages; it is not a first birth registration or proof of one borrowing route in every family.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact German given-name row, not the English surname row. Catalogue Siliņš p69; no universal borrowing route inferred. Exact agency HTML record https://www.personvarduatveide.lv/words/39305?locale=lv was opened; the cited printed manual page was not independently reopened unless separately noted.

records.name: Eligijus
records.facts_used: Eligijus: Lithuanian Eligijus continues Latin Eligius. The family is linked to eligere, to choose, and the interpretation chosen. Its Latin history differs from that of similar-sounding native compound names; familiar-looking syllables are not a separate etymology. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Eligijus (Elys, Ligis) on 1 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Original Salys PDF318/printed303 December1. Historical calendar variants are not all modern calendar entries.
